name: "The Future" Rex Reynolds
caption: The winner of New ERA of Wrestling's ten-man Newcomer Battle Royal, who told the promotion's own Vice President that he was the future of her company hours before he proved it.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 17 February 2005): in a backstage scene he refuses a contract argument with Vice President Juliet Marceau ("you're going to see the future of your company"), then outlasts nine other newcomers in the Newcomer Battle Royal, eliminating Dallas Carter last with a hurricanrana over the top rope. On the 30 May 2005 RAUCOUS he loses the tournament's own second semifinal to Dallas Carter, a Buried Alive match, powerbombed six feet down into the casket from the top of the dirt mound.
tenures.note: Juliet Marceau's own line in that scene places him as having come to New ERA from SWC.

tenures.source: Billed on the promotion's own cards.

name: "The Real Fuckin' Deal" Thomas Lombardi
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling newcomer who reached the PRODIGY Classic Xtreme Championship tournament's semifinals by staying out of a battle royal's way, and by following one opponent under the ring to drag him back out.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 17 February 2005): one of the final three of the Newcomer Battle Royal, advancing to the tournament's semifinals. He eliminates Jenro Electrovolt with a powerbomb over the top rope after chasing him under the ring, and is eliminated last of the three by Rex Reynolds. On the 28 May 2005 RAPTURE he loses the tournament's own first semifinal to Chaos, a Taipei Death Match stopped by the referee with Lombardi bleeding and fading in the Python Lock. His manager Derek is named on the 28 May 2005 RAPTURE.

name: Jenro Electrovolt
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling newcomer who hid under the ring through much of a battle royal until the crowd pointed him out.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 17 February 2005): an entrant in the Newcomer Battle Royal, eliminated by a Thomas Lombardi powerbomb over the top rope after being dragged out from under the ring. He returns on the 28 May 2005 RAPTURE, billed from Kyoto, Japan, and loses to Mr. Entertainment.

name: GBH
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling newcomer, eliminated from the Newcomer Battle Royal by a single flying cross body that took out two men at once.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 17 February 2005): an entrant in the Newcomer Battle Royal, eliminated when Rex Reynolds's flying cross body sent him and Dallas Carter over the top rope together.

identity.note: Name collision only. Another wing carries a one-appearance wrestler of the same name ten days later, in February 2005, and nothing in either promotion's own documents links the two.

name: The North Star
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling newcomer, the second man eliminated from the Newcomer Battle Royal.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 17 February 2005): an entrant in the Newcomer Battle Royal, eliminated by Dallas Carter with a single-leg dump over the top rope.

name: Randy
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling newcomer, the first man out of the Newcomer Battle Royal at roughly thirty-five seconds.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 17 February 2005): an entrant in the Newcomer Battle Royal, eliminated first, by a Riot clothesline while Sean Senn held his legs; the commentary team put his time at about thirty-five seconds.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named wrestler in another wing five years earlier, with nothing in either promotion's own documents linking the two.

name: Riot
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling newcomer, eliminated from the Newcomer Battle Royal by the charge he started himself.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 17 February 2005): an entrant in the Newcomer Battle Royal; he eliminates Randy early, and is himself eliminated when his own charge sends three men over the top rope and he is the only one of them to reach the floor.

identity.note: Name collision only: Riot is a name several promotions have used, and nothing in their documents links any of them to this one.

name: "the Dynasty" Ace McAllister
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling newcomer who threw the first punch of the Newcomer Battle Royal and was suplexed out of it.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 17 February 2005): the entrant who starts the Newcomer Battle Royal with a right hand to GBH, eliminated by a Dallas Carter inverted suplex over the top rope. He returns on the 28 May 2005 RAPTURE for a Fatal Fourway, led to the ring by Jade, and is the first man Trevor Cane clears from it.

name: Jeffords
caption: The Phantom Republican's own security guard in New ERA of Wrestling, who did his employer's ringside work for him.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 17 February 2005): he walks out with the Phantom Republican, blocks DREDD from ringside, chokeslams Jonathan Marx on the arena floor while the referee is distracted, and finally chases John Doe into the ring and splashes him in the corner — the interference that gets the World title shot match thrown out. He walks the Phantom Republican to the ring again on the 30 May 2005 RAUCOUS for New ERA's first Debate Match, stepping between him and the World Champion and shielding him from thrown rubbish. New ERA's own 2006 broadcasts carry the character further: RAUCOUS of 3 February 2006, 5 July 2006, 24 July 2006; BattleBRAWL 2 of 19 September 2006.
The fed's own EPICENTER/GAMEDAY broadcast recaps of this era's own tournaments and shows

name: Madeline
caption: Whisper's own second in New ERA of Wrestling, who also worked Alister Hayze's corner.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 15 January 2005, held show, enrichment-only, not served; its own on-screen EPISODE heading reads RAUCOUS 18): Carl Jacobs announces Whisper for the Women's Championship match as "being led to the ring by Madeline", and she works Whisper's corner, rolling Karla Starr back into the ring and cheering Whisper on. On the 17 February 2005 RAUCOUS the ring announcer bills Alister Hayze and Whisper as "being led to the ring by Madeline" for their mixed tag team match, and she walks back up the ramp celebrating with them afterwards.

name: Felicia Hart
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling competitor who slapped the Women's Champion twice from flat on her back and nearly stole the match with it.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAPTURE broadcast (taped 28 May 2005): billed from Roswell, New Mexico in a non-title match against Women's Champion Karla Starr, kicking out of a Boston Crab and two covers and catching Starr in a small package before losing to a superkick and a moonsault. New ERA's own 2006 broadcasts carry the character further: RAUCOUS of 24 July 2006, 19 December 2006; RAPTURE of 17 December 2006.
the fed's own served show documents, read start to finish — this character is named and staged directly in NFW's own results text
The VENUS Wrestling Alliance's own B1TCHIN' broadcast (30 December 2006) carries the character.

name: Derek
caption: Thomas Lombardi's own manager in New ERA of Wrestling, who brought gauze to one Taipei Death Match and a steel chair to the same one.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAPTURE broadcast (taped 28 May 2005): announced as Thomas Lombardi's manager for the PRODIGY Classic Xtreme Championship tournament semifinal, he wraps Lombardi's bleeding waist at ringside, hits Chaos twice with a steel chair, and is chokeslammed for it.

name: Jade
caption: Ace McAllister's own second in New ERA of Wrestling, who drew a bigger reaction than he did on the way to the ring.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAPTURE broadcast (taped 28 May 2005): the ring announcer bills Ace McAllister as "being led to the ring by Jade" for the Fatal Fourway.

identity.note: Name collision only: another wing carries a Jade who wrestled and held a championship there a year earlier, where this one is a second at ringside, and nothing in either promotion's own documents links them.

name: Nikki Hawke
caption: Jason Hawke's own second in New ERA of Wrestling.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAPTURE broadcast (taped 28 May 2005): the ring announcer bills Jason Hawke as "being led to the ring by Nikki" for the Fatal Fourway; she tends to him in the corner during the match and watches the finish from the floor.
tenures.note: New ERA's own 27 January 2005 RAPTURE had already billed Jason Hawke as led to the ring by his wife, spelling the name Niki; this tenure records the 28 May 2005 spelling the ring announcer used.

name: Carey Elliot
caption: Nick Elliot's wife, who worked his corner in New ERA of Wrestling.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own International Intrigue pay-per-view (taped 20 June 2005, held show, enrichment-only, not served): Nick Elliot walks out for his debut match "along with his wife Carey and Owen", and Carl Jacobs announces him "led to the ring by Carey Elliot and Owen"; Elliot hands Owen his shirt and kisses Carey before the bell, and both are at ringside for the whole match. She is at ringside again for his 19 September 2005 RAUCOUS match, where the ring announcer introduces him "flanked on either side by Carey and Owen".
tenures.note: Billed by the ring announcer under the surname Elliot and described on air as Nick Elliot's wife; recorded as a second.

name: Owen
caption: A second in Nick Elliot's corner in New ERA of Wrestling.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own International Intrigue pay-per-view (taped 20 June 2005, held show, enrichment-only, not served): Nick Elliot walks out for his debut match "along with his wife Carey and Owen", and Carl Jacobs announces him "led to the ring by Carey Elliot and Owen"; Elliot hands Owen his shirt and kisses Carey before the bell, and both are at ringside for the whole match. He is at ringside again for Elliot's 19 September 2005 RAUCOUS match, where the ring announcer introduces Elliot "flanked on either side by Carey and Owen".
tenures.note: Named by first name only, with no billing and no stated role beyond accompanying Nick Elliot; recorded as a second.

name: Kidd Jackson
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling newcomer from the Bronx, New York, who debuted on the July 2006 RAPTURE and was the first man out of its next fatal fourway.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAPTURE broadcast (taped 3 July 2006): billed from the Bronx, New York, he makes his New ERA debut against Chris McMillan and the two are disqualified together for refusing to release their chokeholds. He is the first man eliminated, by an Ozeki avalanche, in the fatal fourway on the 22 July 2006 RAPTURE.

name: Ozeki
caption: New ERA of Wrestling's first sumo wrestler, a 405-pound competitor from Nagoya, Japan, led to the ring by his manager Seth Champion.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAPTURE broadcast (taped 3 July 2006): billed from Nagoya, Japan at 405 pounds, he makes his New ERA debut against Matthew and both men are counted out. He wins the fatal fourway on the 22 July 2006 RAPTURE with the Izumo Thunder, and enters the BattleBRAWL 2 rumble (19 September 2006) at number eighteen, where nine men lift him over the top rope.

name: Seth Champion
caption: Ozeki's manager in New ERA of Wrestling, who cut his promo for the BattleBRAWL 2 rumble.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAPTURE broadcast (taped 3 July 2006): the broadcast describes him as Ozeki's manager and he leads the sumo wrestler to the ring. On the 22 July 2006 RAPTURE he works Ozeki's corner in the fatal fourway and cuts a promo with him for the BattleBRAWL 2 rumble.

name: "Showtime" JR White
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling newcomer from Lima, Ohio, who debuted on the 22 July 2006 RAPTURE and lasted to the final two of its fatal fourway.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAPTURE broadcast (taped 22 July 2006): billed from Lima, Ohio, he makes his New ERA debut in the fatal fourway, eliminates Tommy O'Hagan with the Box Office Smash and is the last man pinned by Ozeki. He enters the BattleBRAWL 2 rumble (19 September 2006) at number eleven and is thrown out by Copycat.

name: "Tommy Gun" Tommy O'Hagan
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling newcomer from Regina, Saskatchewan, who debuted on the 22 July 2006 RAPTURE and entered the BattleBRAWL 2 rumble at number eight.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAPTURE broadcast (taped 22 July 2006): billed from Regina, Saskatchewan, he makes his New ERA debut in the fatal fourway and is eliminated second by JR White. He enters the BattleBRAWL 2 rumble (19 September 2006) at number eight and is dumped with Joey Melton by Shawn Hart.

name: "Sensational" Steven Shane
caption: A New ERA of Wrestling newcomer from Hollywood, California, who debuted at BattleBRAWL 2 by drawing the last number in its rumble.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own BattleBRAWL 2 pay-per-view (taped 19 September 2006): billed from Hollywood, California, he makes his New ERA debut entering the rumble at number twenty. He beats HAL with the California Clutch on the 17 December 2006 RAPTURE, loses to Peter File on the 31 December 2006 RAUCOUS, and is drawn there as challenger for the Television Championship.

identity.note: Name and ring name only. Other wings carry wrestlers billed "Sensational" Steven Shane in the same years, and nothing in New ERA's own documents links them to this one.

name: Candy Carmichael
caption: A newcomer from Beverly Hills, California, introduced backstage on New ERA of Wrestling's RAUCOUS of 19 December 2006 and signed to the VENUS Wrestling Alliance, where she won her first match.

tenures.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 19 December 2006): Victoria Hawke shows her around backstage and the announce team call her New ERA's newest female star. Juliet Marceau names her in the same show among the women whose contracts pass to the VENUS Wrestling Alliance.

The VENUS Wrestling Alliance's own B1TCHIN' broadcast (30 December 2006): billed from Beverly Hills, California, she debuts against Carlee Marx and wins with the Tastes Like Candy running sitdown powerbomb.
